NVDA.text: Nvidia fell about 2.9% as semiconductor stocks pulled back broadly and reports it was helping assemble a roughly $500 billion AI-infrastructure fund added financing-risk concerns; the move was partly sector-led as the Nasdaq and chip index also declined.

AVGO.text: Broadcom fell about 1.3%, ending a seven-day winning streak, with no confirmed new company-specific catalyst; the move largely tracked a broad semiconductor pullback as Nvidia, Qualcomm and Intel also declined.

TSM.text: TSM slipped about 0.4% even after TSMC reported July sales up roughly 45% year over year, as the strong operating update was outweighed by a broader semiconductor selloff.

ASML.text: ASML edged down about 0.4% with the broader chip complex; no new ASML-specific catalyst was confirmed, and the day's weakness was mainly sector-led as semiconductor shares pulled back.

KLAC.text: KLA fell about 2.7% in a broad semiconductor-equipment pullback, moving alongside declines in Applied Materials and Marvell; no distinct KLA-specific catalyst was confirmed.

INTC.text: Intel fell about 4.1% after announcing a $15 billion stock offering to fund general corporate and AI/foundry investment, making dilution and added capital needs the clear company-specific catalyst.

MU.text: Micron fell about 1.9% with the chip sector, with no confirmed new negative company-specific catalyst; the decline appears mainly sector-led as semiconductor shares broadly pulled back.

DDOG.text: Datadog rebounded about 11.5% with no confirmed new company-specific catalyst; after last week's earnings-driven selloff, the move appears to have been a reversal of that reaction rather than a broad-market move, since the Nasdaq fell.

META.text: Meta edged up about 0.5% despite a lower Nasdaq, with no confirmed market-moving company catalyst; the gain was modest enough to look like ordinary stock-specific trading rather than a broad tech move.

PLTR.text: Palantir gained about 1.9%, extending the prior week's earnings-driven surge; no new Monday catalyst was confirmed, so residual momentum from the blowout Q2 report remained the clearest support.

SPCX.text: SpaceX rose about 4.2% and closed above its $135 IPO price as fears of heavy insider selling after the first lockup expiration continued to fade, while enthusiasm around the Terafab chip project supported the rebound.
